organizations.normalization_notes: The historical institution name is preserved. Nicholas Deak's visiting-lecturer role is employment, not attendance.
The institution is modeled as an employer only where a source documents teaching or faculty work; education alone does not establish employment.

organizations.active_dates: active by 1941; later taken over by Deak & Co., Inc. according to the cited scholarly account
organizations.normalization_notes: The historical employer is preserved separately from its later successor. The cited scholarly account identifies it as Deak's employer before enlistment.

organizations.active_dates: reported by UPI as founded in 1940 and disbanded at enlistment; disputed
organizations.normalization_notes: This organization record preserves UPI's prewar-company account without merging it into the postwar Deak & Co., Inc. chronology. Susan Glanz instead dates the later firm's incorporation to 1946 and names Korody and Co., Inc. as Deak's pre-enlistment employer.

affiliations.date_precision: The exact private-identifier Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 992 on June 17, 1943. The code identifies student status but names no school, program, employer or end date.
affiliations.research_notes: Student status is not an employer. No institution or Army-to-OSS sequence is inferred.

affiliations.date_precision: The monograph describes an OSS Arthur R. Dayton as a former vice-president of a California export business and as an export executive before his wartime Baghdad work. It names neither the company nor employment dates, and the Box 173 identity bridge is incomplete.
affiliations.research_notes: This is retained as a review lead, not a public fact. U.S. Steel was Dayton's OSS commercial cover and is not modeled as his pre-OSS employer.

affiliations.date_precision: The scholarly chronology dates the appointment from September 1941, explicitly calls Korody and Co., Inc. Deak's employer before enlistment, and places officer-candidate training at the OSS Paratrooper School in December 1942. The exact employment end date is not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: This is the best-supported last civilian employer. It is not labeled the immediate pre-OSS affiliation because the source places intervening officer-candidate status. UPI gives a conflicting prewar-company account.

affiliations.date_precision: The scholarly article dates the part-time visiting-lecturer appointment to 1940-1942; it does not establish whether it ended before or after the Korody appointment began.
affiliations.research_notes: Employment is explicit. It remains an earlier documented pre-OSS role because the overlap and final sequence are not fully resolved.

affiliations.date_precision: The scholarly article places Deak on the City College faculty in 1941 and gives an hourly pay rate. It does not state the appointment's end date.
affiliations.research_notes: The source documents paid faculty work, so this is employment rather than student status. It is not promoted to the last-employer field.

affiliations.date_precision: UPI reports that Deak founded the company in 1940 and disbanded it when he enlisted. This conflicts with Susan Glanz's file-grounded chronology, which dates Deak & Co., Inc. to 1946 and names Korody and Co., Inc. as the pre-enlistment employer.
affiliations.research_notes: The contradictory chronology is preserved for review and excluded from default analytics.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index supplies Richard A Day Jr. and Box 173 without rank or private identifier. Complete Army, CIA and LoC checks plus exact-name, suffix, OSS, employer, occupation, obituary, institutional, newspaper, directory, military and archival searches produced common-name candidates without two corroborating wartime identifiers.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 173 for full identity, personnel status, occupation, employer and chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified OSS index and official Army merged file agree on James L Dayley's exact full name and private identifier. The Army record documents entry as a private on June 17, 1943 and civilian-occupation code 992, which NARA's code list defines as students.
person_updates.next_action: The Army-entry record documents student status but names no school or employer. Review Box 173 for the institution, any employment, and the Army-to-OSS chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: A scholarly monograph reconstructs OSS Iraq officer Arthur R. Dayton from archival records and describes him as a former California export-business vice-president. The indexed row gives only Arthur Dayton and Box 173, without middle initial, rank or private identifier. Direct OSS context and name make him a plausible lead, but the required second identity bridge is absent, so the occupation candidate remains low confidence and withheld.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 173 for a middle name, birth year, Rutgers or New Jersey link, export-business history and OSS Iraq assignment before accepting Arthur R. Dayton. U.S. Steel was described as OSS cover and must not be recorded as a pre-OSS employer.
